# gledach

> Free, installable tools that turn public data into information, insight and
> intelligence. Run them on your own machine. No account to start.
>
> Featured: signal, slot 01. Track anyone, compare anyone, on your own machine.
> Anyone means any company you name in one file.

gledati (slav.): to watch. What a good analyst does before speaking.

gledach is a shelf, not a platform. The tools published here are written by the
same author but do not share a stack, an interface or a release cadence. What
they share is the promise below.

Look at one before installing it: https://signal.gledach.de is a real signal
deployment exported to one static file, dated and read only. `npm run view` puts
the same dashboard on 127.0.0.1:5180 against your own subject.

## House rules

- Free, and the source is public. MIT unless a dependency makes that impossible.
- Your machine is the runtime. Cloud is for sharing state between machines you own.
- No account to start. Keys, hosted databases and schedules are opt in, later.
- Honest about blind spots. Every tool ships a written audit of what it cannot see.
- Read only until you say otherwise. Paid actions ship disabled, behind a spend ceiling.
- Generated text is labelled as generated. Model output is not verified fact.

## The shelf, in one table

Twelve slots, five filled. The table lists the filled ones and the next empty one.
What each tool watches, and what it hands back.

| Slot | Tool | Watches | Tells you | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 01 | signal | Thirteen public sources around whichever market you name | What changed, scored and attributed, over MCP | Live preview |
| 02 | signal-patterns | Nothing. It is the written reasoning | What is watchable, what it costs, how to build it | Docs |
| 03 | whenrun | Day-ahead power prices and renewable share | The cheapest or greenest window, then starts the job in it | Shipped |
| 04 | phonehome | Every DNS query on your own network | Which device talked where, and when that changed | Shipped |
| 05 | recall | Four public registers, against a list of what you own | Which of your things has a notice, and how sure the match is | Shipped |
| 06 | [UNNAMED] | [UNDECIDED] | [UNDECIDED] | Empty |

## Tools

### signal · rung 04, intelligence · live preview · in focus

Situation: you find out a competitor shipped something when a customer mentions
it.

Competitive intelligence your agents can query. Watches a market, turns public
noise into scored and attributed signals, correlates them into convergences that
several independent publishers corroborate, and exposes the result over MCP.
Ships tracking thirteen AI coding agents and app builders. Node, three runtime
dependencies, no build step, libSQL storage that is a local file by default.

It is the only tool on this shelf whose subject is a list the operator writes.
The other four watch something fixed: a power market, a home network, four
public registers. The landing page opens on signal for that reason, and the
shelf index follows immediately under it.

- Repository: https://github.com/gledach/signals
- Live preview: https://signal.gledach.de (static export of a real deployment, dated, read only)
- Install guide: https://github.com/gledach/signals/blob/main/docs/start.md
- Agent surface (MCP): https://github.com/gledach/signals/blob/main/docs/mcp.md
- Blind spots: https://github.com/gledach/signals/blob/main/docs/blindspots.md
- Licence: MIT. Price: 0. Needs Node 22 or newer, and git.

Install:

    git clone https://github.com/gledach/signals && cd signals
    npm install
    npm run db:migrate
    npm run view

That runs offline on a fresh clone, on Windows, macOS or Linux. An LLM key turns
on classification, battlecards and analyst briefs; without one a keyword
classifier runs instead and everything else still works.

Three steps after it runs:

1. Point it at anyone. `cp config/companies.default.mjs config/companies.local.mjs`.
   The roster is one gitignored file, so upstream can be pulled forever without a
   conflict in the only file that was changed. Feeds, GitHub repository mappings,
   Hacker News queries and classifier collision warnings all derive from it, and
   `npm test` fails if a brand name appears anywhere outside `config/`.
2. Let the agent install it:
   `claude mcp add signal -- node /path/to/signals/mcp-server.mjs`. The repository
   ships AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and five skills, so Codex or Claude Code can clone
   it, migrate the database and wire itself in. Node 22 and git still have to be
   on the machine: an agent can run the commands, it cannot conjure a runtime.
3. Then it feeds whatever asks. `npm run start` is one scheduled pass over every
   watcher. Eight MCP tools and `signal://` resources serve the result to an
   agent, JSON endpoints serve it to anything else, briefs and battlecards come
   out as markdown. All read only: the single tool that spends money ships
   disabled and stays under a ceiling shared with cron.

Compare sets an anchor company against up to three rivals across positioning,
target segment, pricing, strengths and weaknesses, and marks a claim
`[unverified]` where the signal set does not support it.

Figures: 13 sources, 8 MCP tools (read only until a deployment opts in),
3 runtime dependencies, 2,600+ signals stored in the deployment behind the preview.

### signal-patterns · reference

Situation: you want to build one of these, and the hard part is knowing what is
watchable at all.

How to build tools that watch the public web: what is watchable, what it costs,
how to build a watcher, and the engineering decisions that only become obvious
after something has broken. Nothing to install.

- Repository: https://github.com/gledach/signal-patterns
- What is watchable: https://github.com/gledach/signal-patterns/blob/main/sources.md
- What it costs: https://github.com/gledach/signal-patterns/blob/main/techniques.md
- Building a watcher: https://github.com/gledach/signal-patterns/blob/main/building-a-watcher.md
- Being consumable by agents: https://github.com/gledach/signal-patterns/blob/main/agent-integration.md

Thesis: the useful signals are the ones a company exposes before it means to.
Ordered by lead time: infrastructure (weeks), hiring (months, vague),
documentation (hours), changelog (hours), marketing (at launch), press (after).

### whenrun · rung 04, intelligence · shipped

Situation: power can cost three times more in the evening than it does at midday,
and a backup job does not care when it runs.

Run it when the power is cheap. Watches day-ahead electricity prices and the
renewable-share forecast, finds the cheapest or greenest window that still meets
a job's deadline, and starts the job there. The first tool here that acts on what
it sees rather than reporting it.

- Repository: https://github.com/gledach/whenrun
- Running it for real: https://github.com/gledach/whenrun/blob/main/docs/running-it.md
- What it cannot do: https://github.com/gledach/whenrun/blob/main/docs/roadmap.md
- Licence: MIT. Price: 0.

Install:

    git clone https://github.com/gledach/whenrun && cd whenrun
    node bin/whenrun.mjs prices

Figures: 2 keyless price sources, 16 bidding zones, 0 runtime dependencies,
142 offline tests. Savings are reported against the delivered bill rather than
the spot price, because grid fees and tax do not move by the hour.

### phonehome · rung 04, intelligence · shipped

Situation: nothing on a home network tells you where it has been sending data, or
when that changed.

See what your devices talk to. A local DNS resolver that records which domains
every device on your network contacts, classifies them, and says when one starts
talking somewhere new. It does not block and does not upload: finding out is a
different job from filtering. Reads existing Pi-hole, AdGuard Home, dnsmasq or
Unbound logs, so months of history are available without re-pointing a network.

- Repository: https://github.com/gledach/phonehome
- What it cannot do: https://github.com/gledach/phonehome/blob/main/docs/roadmap.md
- Licence: MIT. Price: 0.

Install:

    git clone https://github.com/gledach/phonehome && cd phonehome
    node bin/phonehome.mjs import /var/log/pihole.log --execute
    node bin/phonehome.mjs report

Figures: 4 log formats read, 11 categories, 0 runtime dependencies, 67 offline
tests. "unknown" is kept visible and counted rather than guessed at, and the
share of traffic using encrypted DNS is reported because that traffic routes
around the tool entirely. One category exists for televisions reporting what is
on the screen, because filed under telemetry nobody notices it.

### recall · rung 04, intelligence · shipped

Situation: the notice for the thing in your kitchen was published, and nobody sent
it to you.

Tell me when something I own is recalled. Keeps a list of the things one person
owns and checks it against four public registers, none of which needs an account:
EU Safety Gate (product alerts), BfArM (German medicine supply shortages, which
is availability rather than safety), NHTSA (US vehicle campaigns), and
endoflife.date (software past security support).

- Repository: https://github.com/gledach/recall
- What it cannot do: https://github.com/gledach/recall/blob/main/docs/roadmap.md
- Licence: MIT. Price: 0.

Install:

    git clone https://github.com/gledach/recall && cd recall
    cp config/inventory.default.mjs config/inventory.local.mjs
    node bin/recall.mjs check

Figures: 4 registers, 0 keys, 0 runtime dependencies, 98 offline tests. Also
exposes an MCP server with 5 read-only tools.

Matches are graded rather than binary: exact on a barcode, PZN or VIN; strong
when make and model both appear in a notice; weak when only a distinctive model
number does; mention for noise. Weak is shown by default, because missing the one
that mattered is worse and invisible while a false alarm is merely annoying. A
register that could not be reached is reported as unreachable, never as clean:
"nothing found" and "could not look" must never render the same way, and nothing
in the output ever states that a product is safe.

### Slot 06 · not built

Empty. The shelf is built to hold a dozen. Nothing is planned publicly, and there
is no roadmap to quote.

Requests go to https://github.com/gledach/requests, a public queue. The form asks
the three questions that decide whether a thing is watchable at all: what you
check by hand and how often, where it is published, and whether seeing it needs an
account. Without a GitHub account, request@gledach.de takes the same three
answers, and anything worth building is filed in the queue afterwards, so the list
stays the whole list. A request that would help more people than the person asking
is built first, and the open issues are how you check that.

## The ladder

Stated after the tools, not before them: it is the argument for why each tool
stops where it stops. Every tool moves something public up four rungs and says
where it stopped.

1. Data: what is already public. Feeds, filings, certificate logs, changed pages.
2. Information: collected, deduplicated, attributed.
3. Insight: scored and correlated.
4. Intelligence: queryable by something other than a person.

Most monitoring products stop at rung 02 and call the result a feed.

## Previews

Convention: `<tool>.gledach.de`. One per tool, replaced in place. A preview is a
static export of a real deployment: real data, dated, read only. A re-export
overwrites it, so a preview is the most recent snapshot rather than an archive.
